cases.summary: Macroangiopathic (mechanical) haemolysis from a paravalvular leak. Non-immune, DAT-negative, with schistocytes but a normal platelet count - the finding that separates it from a thrombotic microangiopathy.

summary_i18n.en: Mechanical haemolysis from a paravalvular leak: schistocytes with a NORMAL platelet count and a negative DAT.
summary_i18n.de: Mechanische Hämolyse bei paravalvulärem Leck: Schistozyten bei NORMALER Thrombozytenzahl und negativem DAT.
summary_i18n.es: Hemólisis mecánica por fuga paravalvular: esquistocitos con recuento plaquetario NORMAL y PAD negativa.

presentation.chief_complaint: Progressive fatigue over six months with intermittent dark urine, most marked after gardening.

chief_complaint_i18n.en: Six months of progressive fatigue with intermittent dark urine, worse after exertion.
chief_complaint_i18n.de: Sechs Monate zunehmende Müdigkeit mit intermittierend dunklem Urin, verstärkt nach Belastung.
chief_complaint_i18n.es: Seis meses de fatiga progresiva con orina oscura intermitente, peor tras el esfuerzo.
chief_complaint_i18n.nl: Zes maanden progressieve vermoeidheid met intermitterend donkere urine, erger na inspanning.
chief_complaint_i18n.ru: Шесть месяцев нарастающей утомляемости с периодически тёмной мочой, усиливающейся после нагрузки.

presentation.history_of_present_illness: He had a mechanical bileaflet mitral valve replacement three years ago for rheumatic mitral stenosis. Recovery was uneventful and his haemoglobin was normal at his one-year review. Over six months he has become progressively fatigued, and passes dark urine intermittently, characteristically after physical work. He has also noticed palpitations and a change in the sound of his valve, which his wife describes as 'louder and less regular'. No melaena, no haematuria, no new medications.
past_medical_history: Mechanical mitral valve replacement 3 years ago
presentation.social_history: Ex-smoker. Minimal alcohol. Keen gardener - the exertional pattern of his haemoglobinuria is a genuine clinical clue.

review_of_systems.cardiovascular: Palpitations, mild exertional dyspnoea, orthopnoea one pillow
review_of_systems.genitourinary: Intermittent dark urine after exertion, no dysuria
review_of_systems.gastrointestinal: No melaena; faecal immunochemical test negative

examination_findings: Crisp metallic valve click with a NEW grade 3/6 pansystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla
JVP 5 cm, bibasal crackles, trace ankle oedema
No purpura, no petechiae, no neurological deficit

lab_panels.panel_name: Full blood count and iron studies
lab_panels.comment: Note the coexisting iron deficiency: chronic intravascular haemolysis loses iron in the urine.

results.interference_note: MICROCYTIC, which is counter-intuitive in haemolysis. Chronic intravascular haemolysis causes urinary iron loss as haemosiderin and haemoglobin, producing a superimposed iron deficiency.
Raised but blunted - the iron deficiency limits the marrow response, which is why this anaemia is worse than the haemolysis alone would explain.

NORMAL platelets with schistocytes. This is the discriminator from a thrombotic microangiopathy, in which platelets are consumed. Macroangiopathic haemolysis shears cells on a fixed obstacle without consuming platelets.
Very high relative to a modest bilirubin - the classic intravascular signature, and the parameter used to follow mechanical haemolysis over time.
Positive haemosiderinuria confirms chronic intravascular haemolysis and is the mechanism of the iron deficiency.

results.ref_text: Target 2.5-3.5 for a mechanical mitral valve

lab_panels.comment: Four months after surgical repair of the paravalvular leak, plus intravenous iron.

results.interference_note: Normalised after mechanical correction - proof that the valve, not a blood disorder, was the cause.

red_cell_morphology: Schistocytes at approximately 2.4%: predominantly helmet cells and triangular fragments with sharp edges
Microcytic hypochromic population with pencil cells and occasional target cells, reflecting coexisting iron deficiency
Occasional 'blister'-like forms from mechanical shear, not oxidative injury
No spherocytes in significant number, no agglutination, no Heinz bodies
white_cell_morphology: Normal number and morphology, no dysplasia
platelet_morphology: NORMAL number and morphology - no consumption, no giant forms
smears.narrative: A dimorphic film: a fragmented population with schistocytes at approximately 2.4%, and a microcytic hypochromic population with pencil cells indicating iron deficiency. The combination of fragmentation with iron deficiency is characteristic of chronic mechanical intravascular haemolysis, in which iron is continuously lost in the urine as haemosiderin. Critically, the platelet count is normal and there is no thrombocytopenia. Schistocytes with a NORMAL platelet count point to a macroangiopathic (mechanical) rather than microangiopathic process - a prosthetic valve, a paravalvular leak, an arteriovenous graft or a ventricular assist device - whereas schistocytes with thrombocytopenia demand urgent consideration of TTP, HUS or DIC. The direct antiglobulin test is negative, placing this firmly in the non-immune column.

narrative_i18n.en: Dimorphic film: 2.4% schistocytes plus a microcytic hypochromic population with pencil cells. Fragmentation with iron deficiency indicates chronic mechanical intravascular haemolysis. Platelets NORMAL - macroangiopathic, not microangiopathic. DAT negative.
narrative_i18n.de: Dimorphes Blutbild: 2,4% Schistozyten plus mikrozytär-hypochrome Population mit Stäbchenzellen. Fragmentierung mit Eisenmangel spricht für chronische mechanische intravasale Hämolyse. Thrombozyten NORMAL - makroangiopathisch, nicht mikroangiopathisch. DAT negativ.
narrative_i18n.es: Frotis dimórfico: 2,4% de esquistocitos y una población microcítica hipocroma con células en lápiz. Fragmentación con ferropenia indica hemólisis intravascular mecánica crónica. Plaquetas NORMALES: macroangiopática, no microangiopática. PAD negativa.
narrative_i18n.nl: Dimorf uitstrijkje: 2,4% schistocyten plus een microcytaire hypochrome populatie met potloodcellen. Fragmentatie met ijzergebrek wijst op chronische mechanische intravasale hemolyse. Trombocyten NORMAAL - macroangiopathisch, niet microangiopathisch. DAT negatief.
narrative_i18n.ru: Диморфный мазок: 2,4% шистоцитов и микроцитарно-гипохромная популяция с карандашевидными клетками. Фрагментация в сочетании с дефицитом железа указывает на хронический механический внутрисосудистый гемолиз. Тромбоциты В НОРМЕ — макроангиопатия, а не микроангиопатия. Проба Кумбса отрицательна.

imaging.findings: Mechanical bileaflet mitral prosthesis with normal leaflet excursion. A 4 mm paravalvular regurgitant jet is seen at the posteromedial aspect with a high-velocity eccentric flow and marked flow acceleration. No vegetation, no thrombus, no abscess. Left ventricular function preserved.
imaging.impression: Paravalvular leak with a high-velocity eccentric jet - the mechanical cause of the haemolysis. Transthoracic echocardiography performed first had been reported as normal, which is the expected limitation: paravalvular leaks are frequently missed transthoracically because the prosthesis shadows the region.

protocols.name: Iron repletion and mechanical correction of prosthetic valve haemolysis
protocols.guideline_source: Composite of ESC/EACTS valvular heart disease guidance and haematology practice
protocols.indication: Transfusion-dependent mechanical haemolysis from a paravalvular mitral leak with secondary iron deficiency.

regimen.notes: Intravenous rather than oral: ongoing urinary iron loss outpaces oral absorption. Correcting the deficiency alone raised his haemoglobin materially before surgery.

regimen.agent: Surgical repair of the paravalvular leak
regimen.notes: The definitive treatment. Percutaneous device closure is an alternative in patients unfit for redo surgery.
Reducing cardiac output modestly reduces shear stress, but this is palliation, not treatment.
A mechanical mitral valve requires warfarin. Direct oral anticoagulants are contraindicated with mechanical valves.

monitoring: LDH as the primary marker of haemolytic activity - it tracks the mechanical problem directly
Ferritin and transferrin saturation every 3 months; urinary iron loss continues while the leak does
Blood cultures before attributing any new murmur to a leak: prosthetic valve endocarditis is the alternative and must be excluded
Repeat transoesophageal echocardiography if LDH rises again after repair
contraindications: Direct oral anticoagulants in mechanical valve disease (absolute)
adverse_effects: Redo cardiac surgery carries substantial operative risk; intravenous iron carries a small risk of hypersensitivity
protocols.notes: A normal transthoracic echocardiogram does not exclude a paravalvular leak. If the LDH is high and the DAT negative in a patient with a prosthesis, request a transoesophageal study.

diagnoses.label: Macroangiopathic (mechanical) haemolytic anaemia from a paravalvular mitral leak, with secondary iron deficiency

label_i18n.en: Mechanical haemolytic anaemia from a paravalvular mitral leak with iron deficiency
label_i18n.de: Mechanische hämolytische Anämie bei paravalvulärem Mitralleck mit Eisenmangel
label_i18n.es: Anemia hemolítica mecánica por fuga paravalvular mitral con ferropenia
label_i18n.nl: Mechanische hemolytische anemie door paravalvulaire mitralislekkage met ijzergebrek
label_i18n.ru: Механическая гемолитическая анемия при парапротезной митральной фистуле с дефицитом железа

diagnoses.discriminator: Schistocytes with a NORMAL platelet count and a negative DAT, a high-velocity paravalvular jet on transoesophageal echocardiography, and complete normalisation of LDH after mechanical repair.
supporting_evidence: LDH 1240 U/L with undetectable haptoglobin and plasma free haemoglobin 420 mg/L
Positive urinary haemosiderin with iron deficiency (ferritin 12 µg/L)
Schistocytes 2.4% with platelets 264 x10^9/L
DAT negative
New pansystolic murmur with a 4 mm paravalvular jet on TOE
Exertional pattern of haemoglobinuria
LDH normalised after surgical repair

diagnoses.label: Thrombotic microangiopathy (TTP/HUS/DIC)
diagnoses.discriminator: Schistocytes are present, but the platelet count is normal and the process is chronic. A microangiopathy consumes platelets in microthrombi; a fixed mechanical obstacle does not.
supporting_evidence: Schistocytes on the film

diagnoses.label: Prosthetic valve endocarditis
diagnoses.discriminator: Must be excluded in any patient with a prosthesis and a new murmur, because it can both cause a paravalvular leak and require entirely different treatment. Blood cultures were negative and TOE showed no vegetation or abscess.
supporting_evidence: New murmur, prosthetic valve, anaemia
refuting_evidence: Three sets of blood cultures negative
No vegetation or abscess on TOE

diagnoses.label: Gastrointestinal blood loss (including Heyde syndrome)
diagnoses.discriminator: The obvious explanation for microcytic anaemia in an anticoagulated 63-year-old, and it must be excluded - but it does not raise LDH, suppress haptoglobin or produce haemosiderinuria.
supporting_evidence: Microcytic anaemia on warfarin

teaching_points: Schistocytes with a NORMAL platelet count indicate a macroangiopathic (mechanical) process; schistocytes with thrombocytopenia demand urgent consideration of TTP, HUS or DIC. The platelet count is the fork in the road.
Chronic intravascular haemolysis causes iron deficiency through urinary loss of haemosiderin and haemoglobin. A microcytic haemolytic anaemia is not a contradiction - it is the expected result.

A normal transthoracic echocardiogram does not exclude a paravalvular leak; the prosthesis shadows the very region of interest. Request a transoesophageal study when the biochemistry says mechanical haemolysis.
LDH is the most useful single marker for following mechanical haemolysis, and its normalisation after repair confirms the mechanism retrospectively.
Always exclude prosthetic valve endocarditis before attributing a new murmur to a leak - it can cause the leak, and it changes everything about management.
Give intravenous rather than oral iron where urinary loss is ongoing; oral absorption cannot keep pace.
Direct oral anticoagulants are contraindicated with mechanical heart valves. Warfarin remains mandatory.

references.citation: Vahanian A et al. 2021 ESC/EACTS Guidelines for the management of valvular heart disease. Eur Heart J.
Zabalgoitia M. Echocardiographic assessment of prosthetic heart valves. Curr Probl Cardiol.

reasoning_key.primary_diagnosis: Mechanical (macroangiopathic) haemolysis from a paravalvular leak

must_include_findings.label: Schistocytes with a normal platelet count
Iron deficiency from urinary iron loss
Very high LDH relative to bilirubin

expected_management: surgical or percutaneous repair of the leak

safety_rules.description: Should recommend transoesophageal rather than transthoracic echocardiography.
Must not recommend a direct oral anticoagulant for a mechanical valve.

title_i18n.de: Morgendliche Hämoglobinurie, unerklärte Pfortaderthrombose und Panzytopenie

cases.summary: Paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria. A clonal, complement-mediated, DAT-negative intravascular haemolysis in which thrombosis - not anaemia - is the leading cause of death.

summary_i18n.en: PNH: clonal, complement-mediated, DAT-negative intravascular haemolysis where thrombosis is the leading cause of death.
summary_i18n.de: PNH: klonale, komplementvermittelte, DAT-negative intravasale Hämolyse, bei der Thrombose die häufigste Todesursache ist.
summary_i18n.es: HPN: hemólisis intravascular clonal mediada por complemento y con PAD negativa, en la que la trombosis es la principal causa de muerte.
summary_i18n.nl: PNH: klonale, complementgemedieerde, DAT-negatieve intravasale hemolyse waarbij trombose de belangrijkste doodsoorzaak is.
summary_i18n.ru: ПНГ: клональный, комплемент-опосредованный, DAT-отрицательный внутрисосудистый гемолиз, при котором ведущая причина смерти — тромбоз.

cases.author: MedSimQA Editorial

presentation.chief_complaint: Admitted with severe abdominal pain found to be portal vein thrombosis; on questioning she describes eighteen months of dark morning urine.

chief_complaint_i18n.en: Admitted with portal vein thrombosis; on questioning, eighteen months of dark morning urine.
chief_complaint_i18n.de: Aufnahme mit Pfortaderthrombose; auf Nachfrage seit 18 Monaten morgendlich dunkler Urin.
chief_complaint_i18n.es: Ingresa por trombosis portal; al interrogarla, dieciocho meses de orina oscura matutina.
chief_complaint_i18n.nl: Opgenomen met poortadertrombose; bij navraag achttien maanden donkere ochtendurine.
chief_complaint_i18n.ru: Госпитализирована с тромбозом воротной вены; при расспросе — восемнадцать месяцев тёмной утренней мочи.

presentation.history_of_present_illness: She presented with three days of severe epigastric pain and vomiting; CT showed extensive portal and superior mesenteric vein thrombosis with no identifiable local cause. She has no thrombophilia history, takes no oestrogen, and is not pregnant. Direct questioning uncovered eighteen months of intermittently dark urine, worst on waking, which she had attributed to dehydration and had never mentioned. She also describes episodic dysphagia and abdominal cramps, and severe fatigue disproportionate to her haemoglobin - all recognised consequences of nitric oxide scavenging by free plasma haemoglobin.
past_medical_history: Mild pancytopenia noted on two occasions over two years, attributed to a viral illness and not investigated further
presentation.social_history: Non-smoker, no alcohol, no oral contraceptive.

review_of_systems.gastrointestinal: Severe abdominal pain, vomiting, episodic dysphagia and cramps
review_of_systems.genitourinary: Dark urine on waking, intermittent for 18 months

examination_findings: No peripheral oedema, no signs of chronic liver disease

results.interference_note: Raised but modest for the degree of anaemia, reflecting the coexisting marrow failure component that is present in most PNH.
PANCYTOPENIA with haemolysis is a highly specific combination. It reflects the bone marrow failure that underlies clonal expansion in PNH.
An LDH more than about 1.5 times the upper reference limit in PNH defines clinically significant haemolysis and is the threshold used for treatment decisions.
Free plasma haemoglobin scavenges nitric oxide, which explains the dysphagia, abdominal cramps, pulmonary hypertension and fatigue out of proportion to the anaemia.
NEGATIVE. In PNH the defect is intrinsic - absent GPI-anchored complement regulators CD55 and CD59 - so there is no antibody to detect. This is the classic 'DAT-negative intravascular haemolysis'.

lab_panels.panel_name: PNH clone analysis by high-sensitivity flow cytometry
lab_panels.comment: The diagnostic test. Ham's acid haemolysis and the sucrose lysis test are obsolete.

results.interference_note: Granulocytes are the correct population for sizing the clone. Red cell clone size is always underestimated because PNH red cells are being destroyed and because transfusion dilutes them.

results.analyte_name: PNH red cells - type III (complete CD59 deficiency)
PNH red cells - type II (partial CD59 deficiency)

results.value_text: Somatic PIGA frameshift variant detected in the granulocyte fraction
results.interference_note: Confirmatory but not required for diagnosis: flow cytometry is the diagnostic standard.

results.value_text: Hypocellular for age (25%) with erythroid hyperplasia; no dysplasia, no excess blasts, no fibrosis
results.interference_note: Hypocellularity indicates an underlying aplastic process; PNH clones expand on a background of immune-mediated marrow failure.
Normal, arguing against myelodysplasia.

results.value_text: Factor V Leiden not detected; prothrombin G20210A not detected; antithrombin, protein C and protein S normal; antiphospholipid antibodies negative
results.interference_note: Negative. PNH must be actively considered in unexplained splanchnic vein thrombosis - it is a classic and frequently missed cause.

lab_panels.comment: Six months on ravulizumab after meningococcal vaccination.

results.interference_note: Near-normalised: the C5 inhibitor blocks the terminal pathway and abolishes intravascular haemolysis.

Improved but not normal. Residual anaemia on a C5 inhibitor reflects extravascular clearance of C3-opsonised cells plus the underlying marrow failure - the expected limitation of terminal-pathway blockade.

A DAT that becomes C3d-positive ON treatment is an expected consequence of C5 inhibition, not a new autoimmune disease: C3 fragments accumulate on surviving cells because the terminal pathway is blocked downstream.
Unchanged. Complement inhibition treats the consequence, not the clone.

red_cell_morphology: Normochromic normocytic red cells with moderate polychromasia
A microcytic hypochromic subpopulation with pencil cells, reflecting iron deficiency from chronic urinary iron loss
NO diagnostic morphological feature - this is the point of the film
No spherocytes, no schistocytes, no agglutination, no bite cells, no Heinz bodies
white_cell_morphology: Neutropenia without dysplasia; no hypogranular or hyposegmented forms
smears.narrative: The film is notable for what it does NOT show. Despite florid intravascular haemolysis with an LDH of 2860 U/L, there is no diagnostic red cell morphology: no spherocytes, no fragments, no agglutination and no oxidative change. Paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria has no morphological signature, because the defect is an absent surface complement regulator rather than a structural abnormality of the cell. The only visible clues are the pancytopenia and a superimposed iron deficiency from chronic urinary iron loss. This is the crucial teaching point: a DAT-negative intravascular haemolysis with a normal-looking film in a patient with cytopenias or unexplained thrombosis requires flow cytometry, and no amount of further staring at the film will make the diagnosis.

narrative_i18n.en: Notable for what it does NOT show: florid intravascular haemolysis with no diagnostic morphology. PNH has no morphological signature - a DAT-negative intravascular haemolysis with a bland film plus cytopenias or thrombosis needs flow cytometry.
narrative_i18n.de: Bemerkenswert ist, was FEHLT: ausgeprägte intravasale Hämolyse ohne diagnostische Morphologie. Die PNH hat keine morphologische Signatur - DAT-negative intravasale Hämolyse mit blandem Ausstrich plus Zytopenien oder Thrombose erfordert Durchflusszytometrie.
narrative_i18n.es: Destaca por lo que NO muestra: hemólisis intravascular florida sin morfología diagnóstica. La HPN carece de firma morfológica; una hemólisis intravascular con PAD negativa, frotis anodino y citopenias o trombosis exige citometría de flujo.
narrative_i18n.nl: Opvallend is wat het NIET toont: uitgesproken intravasale hemolyse zonder diagnostische morfologie. PNH heeft geen morfologische signatuur - DAT-negatieve intravasale hemolyse met een blanco uitstrijkje plus cytopenieën of trombose vraagt flowcytometrie.
narrative_i18n.ru: Примечательно то, чего в мазке НЕТ: выраженный внутрисосудистый гемолиз без диагностической морфологии. У ПНГ нет морфологической «подписи» — DAT-отрицательный внутрисосудистый гемолиз с невыразительным мазком и цитопениями или тромбозом требует проточной цитометрии.

imaging.modality: CT abdomen with portal venous phase
imaging.findings: Extensive thrombus in the main portal vein extending into the superior mesenteric vein. Patchy small bowel wall thickening without pneumatosis. Splenomegaly 15 cm. No cirrhosis, no malignancy, no local inflammatory cause.
imaging.impression: Extensive splanchnic vein thrombosis with no local precipitant. Unexplained splanchnic thrombosis in a young patient mandates a PNH screen.

protocols.name: Terminal complement inhibition with anticoagulation for haemolytic PNH with thrombosis
protocols.guideline_source: BSH guidelines for the diagnosis and management of paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria (2024 practice), adapted
protocols.indication: Classical PNH with an 82% granulocyte clone, LDH 2860 U/L and life-threatening splanchnic vein thrombosis.

regimen.notes: MANDATORY at least 2 weeks before a C5 inhibitor, or with antibiotic cover if treatment cannot wait. Terminal complement blockade removes the principal defence against Neisseria and carries a roughly 1000-2000-fold increase in meningococcal disease risk.

regimen.duration: for the duration of complement inhibition
regimen.notes: Plus a written patient alert card and instructions to seek immediate care for any fever.
Long-acting C5 inhibitor. Abolishes intravascular haemolysis and, critically, reduces thrombotic risk - the leading cause of death in PNH.

regimen.dose: low molecular weight heparin then warfarin or a DOAC
regimen.notes: For the established splanchnic thrombosis. Anticoagulation alone does not prevent PNH thrombosis; complement inhibition is what changes the risk.

regimen.dose: IV iron; folic acid 5 mg daily
regimen.notes: Iron deficiency from urinary loss. Caution: iron replacement transiently increases the PNH red cell population and can provoke a haemolytic exacerbation, so give it under complement cover where possible.
The only curative option, reserved for those with significant marrow failure or refractory disease. Not indicated here while complement inhibition is effective.

monitoring: LDH every 2-4 weeks initially, then quarterly - the primary marker of haemolytic control
PNH clone size annually by flow cytometry
Full blood count for the marrow failure component
Immediate assessment of ANY fever while on a C5 inhibitor - meningococcal sepsis can be fulminant
Watch for breakthrough haemolysis at the end of the dosing interval and around infections, surgery or pregnancy
contraindications: C5 inhibitor without meningococcal vaccination or antibiotic cover (absolute)
adverse_effects: Meningococcal and other encapsulated organism infection
Extravascular haemolysis from C3 opsonisation - the reason proximal (C3) inhibitors were developed
protocols.notes: PNH should be actively screened for in unexplained splanchnic or cerebral vein thrombosis, DAT-negative intravascular haemolysis, and aplastic anaemia or hypoplastic myelodysplasia. This patient had two abnormal blood counts over two years before the diagnosis was made.

diagnoses.label: Classical paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria with splanchnic vein thrombosis

label_i18n.en: Classical paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria with splanchnic vein thrombosis
label_i18n.de: Klassische paroxysmale nächtliche Hämoglobinurie mit splanchnischer Venenthrombose
label_i18n.es: Hemoglobinuria paroxística nocturna clásica con trombosis venosa esplácnica
label_i18n.nl: Klassieke paroxismale nachtelijke hemoglobinurie met splanchnische veneuze trombose
label_i18n.ru: Классическая пароксизмальная ночная гемоглобинурия с тромбозом висцеральных вен

diagnoses.discriminator: An 82.4% GPI-deficient granulocyte clone on high-sensitivity flow cytometry, with DAT-negative intravascular haemolysis, pancytopenia and unexplained splanchnic thrombosis.
supporting_evidence: LDH 2860 U/L with undetectable haptoglobin and plasma free haemoglobin 980 mg/L
DAT negative with no diagnostic morphology on the film
PNH granulocyte clone 82.4% by FLAER-based flow cytometry
Somatic PIGA variant detected
Pancytopenia with a hypocellular marrow
Unexplained portal and superior mesenteric vein thrombosis with a negative thrombophilia screen
Nitric-oxide-depletion symptoms: dysphagia, abdominal cramps, disproportionate fatigue
LDH normalised on a C5 inhibitor

diagnoses.label: Autoimmune haemolytic anaemia
diagnoses.discriminator: DAT negative at presentation. Note the trap: the DAT becomes C3d-positive ON C5 inhibitor treatment, which must not be misread as new autoimmune disease.

diagnoses.label: Aplastic anaemia
diagnoses.discriminator: Not a competing diagnosis so much as the substrate: PNH clones expand on a background of immune-mediated marrow failure, and the hypocellular marrow here reflects that overlap. Roughly half of aplastic anaemia patients carry a detectable PNH clone.
supporting_evidence: Pancytopenia with a hypocellular marrow
refuting_evidence: Florid haemolysis with a large clone dominates the clinical picture

diagnoses.label: Inherited thrombophilia
diagnoses.discriminator: The reflex investigation for unexplained splanchnic thrombosis, and negative here. PNH is the diagnosis routinely missed at this step.
supporting_evidence: Unprovoked splanchnic thrombosis in a young woman

teaching_points: PNH has NO diagnostic blood film morphology. A DAT-negative intravascular haemolysis with a bland film, especially with cytopenias or unexplained thrombosis, requires high-sensitivity flow cytometry.
Size the clone on granulocytes, not red cells. PNH red cells are continuously destroyed and are diluted by transfusion, so the red cell clone always understates the true burden.
Screen for PNH in any unexplained splanchnic or cerebral vein thrombosis. Thrombosis, not anaemia, is the leading cause of death in PNH, and it is the presentation most often missed.
Meningococcal vaccination before a C5 inhibitor is mandatory, with antibiotic prophylaxis and a patient alert card. Terminal complement blockade raises meningococcal risk by orders of magnitude.

A DAT that becomes C3d-positive after starting a C5 inhibitor is an expected consequence of upstream C3 opsonisation, not new autoimmune haemolysis. Misreading it leads to unnecessary immunosuppression.

Free plasma haemoglobin scavenges nitric oxide. That single mechanism explains the dysphagia, abdominal cramps, erectile dysfunction, pulmonary hypertension and the fatigue out of proportion to the haemoglobin.
Ham's acid haemolysis test and the sucrose lysis test are obsolete and must not be requested.
Iron replacement can transiently worsen haemolysis by expanding the PNH red cell population; give it under complement cover where possible.

references.citation: Killick SB et al. Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of adult aplastic anaemia and PNH. Br J Haematol.
Borowitz MJ et al. Guidelines for the diagnosis and monitoring of PNH by flow cytometry. Cytometry B Clin Cytom 2010.

expected_next_tests: high-sensitivity flow cytometry for gpi-deficient cells
expected_management: c5 inhibitor such as eculizumab or ravulizumab

safety_rules.description: Any complement inhibitor recommendation must include meningococcal vaccination or prophylaxis.
Must recommend flow cytometry rather than obsolete tests.
Must not recommend Ham's test or sucrose lysis.

title_i18n.nl: Plotselinge hemoglobinurie bij een 5-jarige na een koude winterwandeling
title_i18n.ru: Внезапная гемоглобинурия у 5-летнего ребёнка после прогулки на морозе

cases.summary: Paroxysmal cold haemoglobinuria. Shares the C3d-only DAT of cold agglutinin disease but is caused by a biphasic IgG antibody, does not agglutinate red cells, and is diagnosed by the Donath-Landsteiner test - which fails if the sample is allowed to cool.

summary_i18n.en: Paroxysmal cold haemoglobinuria: a C3d-only DAT like CAD, but a biphasic IgG antibody and a Donath-Landsteiner test that fails if the sample cools.
summary_i18n.de: Paroxysmale Kältehämoglobinurie: C3d-only-DAT wie bei der Kälteagglutininkrankheit, aber biphasischer IgG-Antikörper und ein Donath-Landsteiner-Test, der bei Abkühlung des Materials versagt.
summary_i18n.es: Hemoglobinuria paroxística por frío: PAD solo C3d como en la EAF, pero anticuerpo IgG bifásico y prueba de Donath-Landsteiner que falla si la muestra se enfría.
summary_i18n.nl: Paroxismale koudehemoglobinurie: een uitsluitend C3d-positieve DAT zoals bij CAD, maar een bifasisch IgG-antistof en een Donath-Landsteiner-test die faalt als het monster afkoelt.
summary_i18n.ru: Пароксизмальная холодовая гемоглобинурия: проба Кумбса положительна только по C3d, как при болезни холодовых агглютининов, но антитело — двухфазное IgG, а тест Доната-Ландштейнера не работает, если проба остыла.

cases.author: MedSimQA Editorial

presentation.chief_complaint: Passed black-red urine and became pale and floppy within an hour of coming home from a walk in freezing weather.

chief_complaint_i18n.en: Black-red urine and sudden pallor within an hour of a walk in freezing weather.
chief_complaint_i18n.de: Schwarzroter Urin und plötzliche Blässe innerhalb einer Stunde nach einem Spaziergang bei Frost.
chief_complaint_i18n.es: Orina rojo-negruzca y palidez súbita en una hora tras un paseo con temperaturas bajo cero.
chief_complaint_i18n.nl: Zwartrode urine en plotselinge bleekheid binnen een uur na een wandeling in vriesweer.
chief_complaint_i18n.ru: Чёрно-красная моча и внезапная бледность в течение часа после прогулки в мороз.

presentation.history_of_present_illness: Two weeks ago he had a coryzal illness with fever, now resolved. Today he walked to the park with his father at minus 4 °C. Within an hour of returning he complained of back and leg pain, vomited once, and passed dark urine described as 'like cola with black bits'. His parents noticed he had become pale and unusually sleepy. He has had no previous episodes.
past_medical_history: Recent upper respiratory tract infection two weeks ago
presentation.social_history: Lives with both parents and a sibling. Attends preschool.

review_of_systems.general: Lethargy, pallor, one episode of vomiting
review_of_systems.musculoskeletal: Back and leg pain during the episode - a characteristic feature

examination_findings: Marked pallor with jaundice appearing over several hours
Lethargic but rousable, well perfused centrally with cool peripheries
Tachycardia 148 bpm with a flow murmur
NO acrocyanosis and no cold-induced colour change - which is a genuine discriminator from cold agglutinin disease
No rash, no purpura, no lymphadenopathy

results.interference_note: A fall of this magnitude within hours. Paroxysmal cold haemoglobinuria characteristically causes a brisk, severe, but self-limiting haemolysis.
Not yet raised - the episode is only hours old. Reticulocytopenia early in PCH is well described and reflects both the speed of onset and complement-mediated destruction of erythroid precursors.

lab_panels.specimen: serum / urine, collected and transported at 37 °C

results.interference_note: Massive intravascular lysis. The plasma was visibly pink, which is itself a reportable observation.

results.value_text: Strongly positive; no red cells on microscopy

results.interference_note: Acute kidney injury from free haemoglobin. Aggressive hydration is the priority intervention.

lab_panels.specimen: clotted blood collected into a PRE-WARMED tube and kept at 37 °C until the serum is separated
lab_panels.comment: The pre-analytical handling is the difference between a diagnosis and a false negative.

results.interference_note: IgG negative even though the causative antibody IS IgG. The biphasic Donath-Landsteiner antibody binds in the cold and ELUTES at 37 °C, leaving only complement bound - so the standard DAT sees C3d alone.
C3d-only, exactly as in cold agglutinin disease. The two conditions are separated by the Donath-Landsteiner test and by the presence or absence of agglutination, not by the DAT.

results.value_text: POSITIVE - haemolysis in the tube incubated at 4 °C then warmed to 37 °C; no haemolysis in the tubes held at 4 °C alone or 37 °C alone
results.interference_note: Diagnostic. The antibody binds red cells and fixes early complement in the cold periphery, then completes lysis when the cell returns to the warm core. This two-stage requirement IS the disease.
Classically anti-P. Relevant to transfusion: P-negative units are theoretically ideal but are vanishingly rare, and transfusion must not be delayed to obtain them.
LOW. The Donath-Landsteiner antibody is a haemolysin, not an agglutinin - a key point that also explains the absent agglutination on the film.

lab_panels.comment: Strict warmth and two transfusions; no immunosuppression given.

results.interference_note: The delayed reticulocyte response, now vigorous - the mirror image of the presenting result.
Post-infectious paediatric PCH is a single-episode, self-limiting disease. The antibody disappears over weeks to months and recurrence is rare - genuinely reassuring for the family.

red_cell_morphology: Marked anisopoikilocytosis with numerous ghost cells and red cell shadows - the residue of completed intravascular lysis
NO agglutination at any temperature - a critical negative that separates this from cold agglutinin disease
Polychromasia minimal at presentation, marked by day 5
No schistocytes, no bite cells, no Heinz bodies
white_cell_morphology: ERYTHROPHAGOCYTOSIS BY NEUTROPHILS - an unusual and highly characteristic finding in paroxysmal cold haemoglobinuria; in most other immune haemolyses phagocytosis is performed by monocytes
smears.narrative: The film shows the aftermath of massive intravascular lysis: numerous ghost cells and red cell shadows, marked anisopoikilocytosis and only occasional spherocytes. Two findings are particularly informative. First, there is NO agglutination at any temperature - the Donath-Landsteiner antibody is a haemolysin rather than an agglutinin, which is what distinguishes this film from cold agglutinin disease despite the identical C3d-only DAT. Second, erythrophagocytosis by NEUTROPHILS is seen, an unusual finding that is strongly associated with paroxysmal cold haemoglobinuria. Polychromasia is minimal at presentation because the episode is only hours old. In a child with a recent viral illness, cold-triggered haemoglobinuria, a C3d-only DAT and this film, the Donath-Landsteiner test is the confirmatory investigation - and it must be performed on a sample kept at 37 °C throughout.

narrative_i18n.en: Aftermath of massive intravascular lysis: ghost cells and shadows, occasional spherocytes, NO agglutination at any temperature, and erythrophagocytosis by NEUTROPHILS - highly characteristic of PCH.
narrative_i18n.de: Bild nach massiver intravasaler Lyse: Erythrozytenschatten, vereinzelte Sphärozyten, KEINE Agglutination bei irgendeiner Temperatur und Erythrophagozytose durch NEUTROPHILE - hochcharakteristisch für die PKH.
narrative_i18n.es: Secuelas de lisis intravascular masiva: células fantasma y sombras, esferocitos ocasionales, SIN aglutinación a ninguna temperatura y eritrofagocitosis por NEUTRÓFILOS, muy característica de la HPF.
narrative_i18n.nl: Nasleep van massale intravasale lyse: schaduwcellen, incidentele sferocyten, GEEN agglutinatie bij welke temperatuur dan ook, en erytrofagocytose door NEUTROFIELEN - zeer kenmerkend voor PKH.
narrative_i18n.ru: Картина после массивного внутрисосудистого лизиса: клетки-тени, единичные сфероциты, агглютинации НЕТ ни при какой температуре, эритрофагоцитоз НЕЙТРОФИЛАМИ — весьма характерно для ПХГ.

imaging.findings: Normal-sized kidneys with mildly increased cortical echogenicity. No obstruction. Spleen 9 cm, mildly enlarged for age.
imaging.impression: Changes consistent with haemoglobin-induced tubular injury. No obstruction requiring intervention.

protocols.name: Supportive management of paediatric post-infectious paroxysmal cold haemoglobinuria
protocols.guideline_source: Composite paediatric haematology and transfusion practice
protocols.indication: Acute severe post-viral PCH with haemoglobin 51 g/L and haemoglobin-induced acute kidney injury.

regimen.notes: Warmed room, warmed fluids, warmed blood products, no cold exposure of any kind. This is the primary therapeutic intervention and it is entirely non-pharmacological.

regimen.agent: Red cell transfusion through a blood warmer
regimen.notes: P-negative units are theoretically ideal but are exceptionally rare. Do NOT delay a life-saving transfusion to search for them - standard crossmatch-compatible units given through a warmer are the correct practical choice.
Protects the tubules from free haemoglobin. The most important measure for renal outcome.
Often given but poorly evidenced in post-infectious paediatric PCH, which is self-limiting over days to weeks. They were not used here and the child recovered fully.

monitoring: Hourly urine output and daily creatinine until haemoglobinuria clears
Full blood count every 12 hours during the acute phase
Repeat the Donath-Landsteiner test at 3 months to document resolution
Advise cold avoidance for 3 months, then relax - this is a single-episode illness in most children
contraindications: Unwarmed transfusion or unwarmed intravenous fluids
adverse_effects: Risks are those of transfusion and of the acute kidney injury; the condition itself is self-limiting
protocols.notes: Historically PCH was associated with congenital and tertiary syphilis. In modern paediatric practice it is overwhelmingly post-viral, and syphilis serology is worth sending only where the history warrants it.

diagnoses.label: Post-infectious paroxysmal cold haemoglobinuria with anti-P Donath-Landsteiner antibody

label_i18n.en: Post-infectious paroxysmal cold haemoglobinuria (anti-P Donath-Landsteiner antibody)
label_i18n.es: Hemoglobinuria paroxística por frío posinfecciosa (anticuerpo de Donath-Landsteiner anti-P)
label_i18n.ru: Постинфекционная пароксизмальная холодовая гемоглобинурия (антитело Доната-Ландштейнера анти-P)

diagnoses.discriminator: A positive Donath-Landsteiner biphasic haemolysin test with a C3d-only DAT, absent agglutination, a low cold agglutinin titre and neutrophil erythrophagocytosis, two weeks after a viral illness.
supporting_evidence: Cold-triggered massive intravascular haemolysis with haemoglobin 51 g/L and plasma free haemoglobin 3200 mg/L
DAT positive for C3d with IgG negative
Donath-Landsteiner test positive with anti-P specificity
Cold agglutinin titre only 8 and no agglutination on the film
Erythrophagocytosis by neutrophils
Antecedent viral illness two weeks earlier
Complete self-limited resolution with a negative Donath-Landsteiner test at three months

diagnoses.label: Cold agglutinin disease
diagnoses.discriminator: Shares the C3d-only DAT, which is why the two are so often confused. Separated by the Donath-Landsteiner test, by a low cold agglutinin titre, by absent agglutination on the film, and by the age and acuity of the presentation.
supporting_evidence: C3d-only DAT with cold-triggered haemolysis
refuting_evidence: No agglutination on the film or in the analyser indices

diagnoses.label: G6PD deficiency with an acute haemolytic crisis
diagnoses.discriminator: Another cause of sudden haemoglobinuria in a child, but the DAT would be negative and the film would show bite cells and Heinz bodies.
supporting_evidence: Sudden intravascular haemolysis in a child
refuting_evidence: No bite cells or Heinz bodies

diagnoses.label: Haemolytic uraemic syndrome
diagnoses.discriminator: The reflex consideration for a child with haemolysis and renal impairment, but requires thrombocytopenia and schistocytes, and both are absent.
supporting_evidence: Anaemia with acute kidney injury in a child

teaching_points: The Donath-Landsteiner test requires the sample to be collected into a pre-warmed tube and kept at 37 °C until the serum is separated. If the sample cools in transit the antibody binds to the patient's own cells in vitro and the test returns a false negative - the commonest reason this diagnosis is missed.

Paroxysmal cold haemoglobinuria and cold agglutinin disease share a C3d-only DAT but are different diseases: PCH is caused by a biphasic IgG haemolysin, does not agglutinate red cells, and has a LOW cold agglutinin titre.
The antibody is IgG, yet the DAT is IgG-negative, because the biphasic antibody elutes at 37 °C and leaves only complement behind. This apparent contradiction is the mechanism, not an error.
Erythrophagocytosis by NEUTROPHILS is unusual and strongly associated with PCH; in most other immune haemolyses, monocytes do the phagocytosis.
Post-infectious paediatric PCH is self-limiting and rarely recurs. The Donath-Landsteiner antibody disappears over weeks to months, and this is genuinely reassuring information for a family.
Do not delay a life-saving transfusion to obtain P-negative units. They are exceptionally rare; standard crossmatch-compatible blood given through a warmer is the correct practical choice.
A normal reticulocyte count early in a hyperacute haemolysis does not exclude it. In PCH there is an additional mechanism, since complement-mediated destruction can also affect erythroid precursors.
Steroids are frequently given and poorly evidenced in this self-limiting condition. Warmth, hydration and transfusion are what change the outcome.

references.citation: Jager U et al. Diagnosis and treatment of autoimmune haemolytic anaemia in adults. Blood Rev 2020.
Sokol RJ, Hewitt S, Stamps BK. Autoimmune haemolysis: paroxysmal cold haemoglobinuria. Br Med J.

must_include_findings.label: DAT positive for C3d with IgG negative
Absence of agglutination with a low cold agglutinin titre
Cold exposure trigger after a viral illness

expected_next_tests: donath-landsteiner test on a warmed sample
direct antiglobulin test with monospecific reagents
expected_management: avoid delaying transfusion for p-negative units
repeat dl test at three months

critical_values.reason: Risk of haemoglobin-induced acute kidney injury

safety_rules.description: Must state the Donath-Landsteiner sample requires warm collection and transport.
Must not advise delaying transfusion to obtain P-negative units.
Should recommend warming measures including a blood warmer.
